newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish government body approves new banking law.
newsitem.headline: Polish government body approves new banking law.

text.p: The Polish government's economic committee (KERM) approved on Monday a draft of a new banking law to replace an outdated law dating from the start of market reforms in 1991.

Janusz Krzyzewski, head of the NBP's legal department told reporters after the committee's meeting that the National Bank of Poland and the finance ministry had reached a compromise on the placement of banking supervision.

"All snags between the NBP and the ministry have been worked out. The banking supervision board will stay within the central bank, but it will be appointed in such a way that the NBP will not have an overwhelming influence upon it," he said.
The board would be chaired by the NBP president and would be composed of representatives of the government, the Securities Commission and insurance supervision.

"If the council of ministers approves this draft, then the government could amend the law on the National Bank of Poland and withdraw its support for the draft law on the NBP proposed by deputies from the ruling coalition," Krzyzewski said.

Deputies from the left-wing coalition of the ex-communist Democratic Left Alliance and the Peasant Party want banking supervision to be carved out of the independent central bank and subordinated to the prime minister.
NBP president Hanna Gronkiewicz-Waltz has warned such a move would likely result in more irregularities in the operation of banks and the weakening of the whole sector.
Krzyzewski said the only problem which still had to be solved was whether or not to allow prosecutors access to data protected by banking secrecy laws.
